title: Internet access is broken when switching between networks on Android
body:
### What is the issue?

Every so often, Tailscale breaks the Internet on my phone. Turning off Tailscale fixes it. While it's on, I get SSL configuration errors in Chrome for any website.

### Steps to reproduce

Unsure. [This Reddit thread](https://<redacted-host>/r/Tailscale/comments/1or92it/tailscale_blocking_internet/?utm_source=share&utm_medium=web3x&utm_name=web3xcss&utm_term=1&utm_content=share_button) says it happens when they switch between networks, but I haven't had that happen reliably.

### Are there any recent changes that introduced the issue?

_No response_

### OS

Android

### OS version

Android 16

### Tailscale version

1.90.4

### Other software

N/A

### Bug report

BUG-56717149e208c661627c62b487f1733859f512ae45106b5121dfb541c89f628e-20251114005845Z-e5d8b06192d129ec

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
** Possible Root Cause ** 

After looking at the reddit thread I did some basic testing to get some insight. I've concluded TS does not notice the network state changes - thus holds the internal routing/connection state with the last known state info. So even if you you got it going on mobile data, if you reassociated via roaming/prioritization, you are "offline" again because your old state is no longer valid. If you toggle the VPN on and off, this refreshes the internal TS routing and you are good until it changes again. 

I highly suspect this has something to do with the new Android Auto HFP mess. Not specifically HFP, but whatever they did under the hood within the last week that requires those who preferred wired only connections with phone calls disabled to enable Bluetooth anyway. I think this is a lower level bug in the core network stack. 1.90.4 was running fine for two weeks, I have narrowed down the bad actor to [this](https://support.google.com/product-documentation/answer/14343500?hl=en) - specifically the "Stability Fixes" if my theory is correct. If I had a rooted phone or a dev emulator already running I would test this right now but I don't have time.
